messages:
Maria Chen: FYI escalation from customer running Redwood Private behind their k8s ingress — they started seeing intermittent 429s and a big jump in p99 latency after switching to their customer-managed gateway this morning. says it correlates with traffic spikes from a batch job. attaching initial logs below.

Aj Patel: thanks — which customer / tenant id? any recent config changes to ingress or rate-limiter?

Maria Chen: tenant id: tenant-acme-42. They migrated to our onprem package + their own gateway yesterday. ingress controller: envoy via the vendor-provided gateway (k8s DaemonSet). they shared their envoy local rate limit section and nginx-style ingress annotations (see below). no pod autoscaler changes.

Devon Lee: can you paste the actual envoy local rate limit config and the k8s annotations? common culprit is tiny token bucket + high burst from the batch job.

Maria Chen: pasted:
```yaml
annotations:
  networking.k8s.io/proxy-read-timeout: "60"
  example.com/ratelimit: "global=100/s,burst=200"
---
# envoy filter snippet
http_filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.local_ratelimit.v3.LocalRateLimit
    stat_prefix: http_local_rate_limiter
    token_bucket:
      max_tokens: 200
      tokens_per_fill: 100
      fill_interval: 5s
    filter_enabled:
      runtime_key: local_rate_limit_enabled
      default_value: true
```

Nora Kim: aha. token_bucket max_tokens 200 with fill 5s and tokens_per_fill 100 means refill is very slow (100 tokens every 5s). if a burst hits >200 tokens it's going to 429 immediately and then p99 spikes. the client batch likely emits a short spike >200 tokens.

Aj Patel: do they also have global rate limit service (RLS) upstream or only local rate limit? local only would explain immediate 429s on that host.

Maria Chen: only local rate limit configured on the gateway. they said we previously ran hosted and never saw this pattern.

Devon Lee: recommended immediate mitigation options:
- increase max_tokens to handle expected burst (e.g., 5000) or tokens_per_fill smaller and fill_interval shorter (e.g., tokens_per_fill: 50, fill_interval: 500ms).
- add a per-client/route hash_key to avoid single-host exhaustion if they have many hosts behind gateway.
- enable 429 Retry-After header from our gateway so clients back off gracefully.

SRE Bot: New support case created: #SUP-2026-241 (automated). Priority: P2. Assigned: Maria Chen.

Maria Chen: customer asked for a low-risk immediate tweak we can recommend. they don't want to re-deploy gateway config during business hours, prefer config map change or helm patch.

Nora Kim: simplest low-risk change: reduce tokens_per_fill and fill_interval via envoy runtime flags if their deployment exposes runtime xDS or will accept a dynamic config roll. example quick patch: set:
```yaml
token_bucket:
  max_tokens: 2000
  tokens_per_fill: 200
  fill_interval: 1s
```
This lets bursts up to 2k and refills faster. should drop 429s for typical batch spikes.

Devon Lee: also suggest adding a client-side smoothing rule: if they control the batch job, throttle with jitter or add small sleeps between concurrent workers. that reduces peak and keeps p99 down.

Aj Patel: can you capture metrics for the gateway where 429s observed? we want per-host local_rate_limited_count, upstream success rates, and request size distribution. If they can share Grafana dashboard link we'll check.

Maria Chen: they gave prometheus endpoint and grafana link. I pulled these metrics: local_rate_limited_count spikes align exactly with batch window. qps peaked at ~12k for 12s on a single gateway node. average request token cost ~1. p50 latency unaffected, p99 jumps from 280ms -> 3.2s.

Nora Kim: 12k qps sustained for 12s on one host with max_tokens 200 explains it. token bucket semantics: you can serve up to max_tokens immediately, then you only get tokens_per_fill every fill_interval. so they exhausted bucket in <1s and then got 429s until refill.

Devon Lee: long-term suggestions:
- move to a global rate limit service (RLS) which coordinates across hosts and avoids single-host exhaustion, with Redis-backed quotas.
- enable request-level keying (per-customer or per-api-key) to distribute load fairly.
- autoscale gateway pods horizontally for batch windows. HPA on the DaemonSet isn't possible; consider Deployment with sufficient node pool or vertical scale.

Aj Patel: short-term patch steps for them (what to run):
1) edit envoy config map / helm values, bump token_bucket to above suggestion.
2) add annotation to ingress to set per-client limit (example below).
3) redeploy gateway with a rolling restart (do one node at a time).

Maria Chen: wrote an example snippet to share with customer:
```yaml
# ingress annotation example (vendor gateway supports this annotation):
annotations:
  example.com/ratelimit: "key=api_key,requests_per_unit=10000,unit=60s"

# envoy local rate limit values we recommend for now:
token_bucket:
  max_tokens: 5000
  tokens_per_fill: 500
  fill_interval: 1s
```

Nora Kim: and ask them to enable the `x-rate-limit-remaining` and `retry-after` headers if supported. helps clients throttle correctly.

SRE Bot: Reminder: mark mitigation actions in case file and state if customer applies patch.

Maria Chen: customer applied a conservative patch (max_tokens: 2000, tokens_per_fill: 200, fill_interval: 1s) during a short maintenance window. they report 429 count dropped by 95% and p99 improved to 420ms.

Devon Lee: great. follow-ups for next week:
- assist them to evaluate moving to global RLS or per-key token buckets.
- include a playbook section in our private docs for 'onprem gateway: token_bucket tuning' with sample knobs and expected effects.

Aj Patel: also add a note about observability: include metrics to detect bucket exhaustion early (rate_limiter_exhausted_count, gap between qps and served qps). set alert: local_rate_limited_count > X over 1m.

Maria Chen: filing internal doc ticket for playbook. closing this thread once I confirm final post-patch metrics. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Nora Kim: quick snippet for the playbook I'll add to the doc:
- Symptom: sudden p99 spike while p50 stable, 429s observed, aligns with short high-qps window.
- Likely cause: local token bucket max_tokens too low or fill interval too long.
- Quick test: run `curl` at same qps profile for 20s to reproduce against a single gateway node.
- Remediation: increase max_tokens OR reduce fill_interval/tokens_per_fill, add per-key hashing, consider global RLS.

SRE Bot: Case #SUP-2026-241 updated: mitigation applied by customer, monitoring in progress.

Maria Chen: closing notes — customer will schedule follow-up to discuss RLS. marking resolved for now but will reopen if we see regressions.
